_provenance.notes: The North Pacific groundfish observer program is the most comprehensive commercial fishery monitoring program in the world. Mandatory 100% observer coverage on large vessels (>60 ft) in federal waters — catching and measuring every fish, crab, and seabird that comes up in the net. The program documents ~500,000 tow observations per year. Bycatch in Alaska groundfish fisheries is low by international standards (0.5-2% of target catch), but the absolute numbers are large given the fishery scale: ~100,000 Chinook salmon, 500,000 halibut, and 20+ million lbs of non-pollock species caught incidentally each year.

chinook_salmon_psc.description: Chinook salmon PSC cap in EBS pollock and GOA groundfish fisheries

annual.notes: Pre-AFA — derby fishing produced higher bycatch rates
Low pollock effort — COVID + low pollock runs

halibut_psc.description: Pacific halibut caught as bycatch in groundfish trawl fisheries — regulated under IPHC + NPFMC
halibut_psc.notes: Halibut bycatch is one of the most contentious issues in Alaska fisheries — sport and commercial IFQ halibut fishermen argue that groundfish trawlers are 'wasting' valuable halibut. The PSC limits for halibut have been reduced multiple times under NPFMC pressure.

annual.notes: AFA begins reducing trawl effort in some areas

seabird_bycatch.description: Seabird incidental take in longline and trawl fisheries — required monitoring under Migratory Bird Treaty Act

annual.notes: Pre-mitigation peak. Short-tailed albatross critically endangered.
Streamer lines beginning to be deployed

mitigation_measures: Weighted branch lines (sink lure below surface quickly)
Streamer lines (bird scaring lines) deployed during setting
Mandatory gear workshop training for longline vessel operators

crab_bycatch_trawl.description: Snow crab and king crab caught as bycatch in EBS trawl fisheries
crab_bycatch_trawl.notes: Crab bycatch from trawl fisheries has become increasingly important as the Bering Sea snow crab population collapsed 2019-2021. Environmentalists and crab fishermen argued that crab bycatch from pollock trawlers contributed to the collapse, though NOAA analysis concludes bycatch was a minor factor vs. the thermal habitat collapse.

snow_crab_trawl_bycatch.2015: ~32 million snow crab (mostly juveniles) — mortality rate disputed
snow_crab_trawl_bycatch.2020: Bycatch reduced as pollock effort shifted; still ~12 million crabs
snow_crab_trawl_bycatch.notes: Most juvenile crab are returned alive, but survival rate is 20-50% — significant mortality in aggregate
